column8: First-time mother packing on the day of her induction; lists what she has.
column9: Anything else that might be helpful? What will the hospital provide for baby? I assume diapers while we are there

column8: Due in a week; plans to stay with her parents after the birth, with a dog to manage.
column9: After the baby is born, my husband and I plan to stay at my parents’ house for a few weeks. They’re creating a guest room for us and helping us transition into parenthood, which we’re incredibly grateful for.

column8: Her husband objects to crating the dog at her parents' house.
column9: I understand his point, but I also feel that if we’re accepting my parents’ help, we need to respect their rules.

column8: At 29 weeks with a 15-month-old.
column9: I. Am. So. Tired. I feel so heavy. I feel like no matter how much sleep I get, I’m still exhausted. Picking up my toddler is hard.

column8: Comparing this pregnancy with her first.
column9: I genuinely don’t remember being this tired with my first but granted I didn’t have a toddler to chase around all day. I’m just PRAYING that newborn tired is going to be so much more manageable.

column8: At 30 weeks with a 4- and 2-year-old; after a growth scan she came home to do bedtime alone.
column9: When I got home I had my usual task of putting the kids to bed and my 4yo was keeping my 2yo awake by chatting so I set him up with books outside whilst I got the other to sleep. Meanwhile my husband is drinking and chatting with his mates on a call.

column8: Deciding to push her husband to take on bedtime before the third baby.
column9: I think I firmly need to push back for AT LEAST bed time. He's going to have to do it anyway when the baby comes. I am not doing 3 bedtimes.

column8: On her usual week.
column9: But otherwise, yes, I do feel like a solo parent most of the time. And allocated all the chores that I didn't ask for. It's just someone has to do them.

column8: Why her husband thinks the housework is hers.
column9: But because I am a SAHM and he is the "breadwinner", he thinks I should do it all I guess. Which at the moment, is impossible.

column8: A tool she would like to use with her husband.
column9: I would love to sit down with him and do that Fair Play card game with him to show him how much work there is in the home and how much I do of it. I'm not sure if he would be bothered or take anything on board.

column8: His word for her requests.
column9: But it is normal for him not to help out with bed time and cleaning around the house. I have "nagged" (his words) so much but he hasn't started to help out.

column8: First pregnancy; friends with two young children compete over hardship.
column9: The "just wait" and "I have no sympathy for you" comments are getting tougher to be around. They invalidate anything and everything my husband and I talk about

column8: The friends, who have no family nearby, lean on the couple for help.
column9: they like to remind us that "we have help and they dont." It makes me feel guilty when we can't meet their expectations

column8: What the friend said to her husband after his workday.
column9: I could not believe those words were barked at my husband when he was talking about his day spent doing manual labor. "I have no sympathy for you."

column8: Almost 6 weeks into her second pregnancy, very sick, waiting on insurance.
column9: My insurance is requiring a prior authorization for me to get Zofran, so I can't get it until it gets approved.

column8: The trip ahead with nausea.
column9: I literally go to the beach in less than 24 hours and have to sit through a 5 hour car ride with my husband, toddler, and sister.

column8: First-time father in West Virginia with a new house and a baby due in September.
column9: We’re excited, nervous, and realizing we have absolutely no idea what life is about to cost once this tiny human arrives.

column8: He wants real spending stories, not averages.
column9: Not looking for internet averages or perfect budgeting advice, just real experiences. What did you spend money on that was worth it? What did you buy and never use? What caught you completely off guard?

column8: His savings plan before the birth.
column9: My wife will be stay home mom but I don’t have much savings. Will eventually need 20k in house repairs which are known before buying. So before baby comes I will have 8-10k saved hopefully provided no house repairs required.

column8: First-time mother at 33 weeks with faint spells; posted in two subs.
column9: Idk if anyone else has experienced this but I’m pretty much at a loss of what it could be, and extremely frustrated as this has caused me to leave work early on multiple occasions.

column8: First pregnancy at 22 weeks, frightened by NHS maternity stories and news coverage.
column9: I’ve heard sooo many scary stories about the NHS maternity care recently and I’m very scared now to actually give birth... today’s article from Sky has not helped… sky calling it breaking point the UK’s maternal crisis.

column8: Why she wants to prepare despite the fear.
column9: I also don’t want to stress about it, but too much is at risk to not be prepared and walk into this blindly

column8: How she copes with frightening stories.
column9: I skip any horror stories I see online as I just don’t want to knowwww

column8: Avoiding stories doesn't shield her from the news.
column9: I don’t really watch or listen to any scary stories but the articles haven’t helped either

column8: Left NHS triage at 1am after hours waiting.
column9: at 1am I self discharged as 3 women were ahead of me and hadnt been seen and waiting in a AC room was just making me feel worse.
